findings.summary: The packet does not establish an executable v8.6.4 release-lock sequence tying the final tag to synchronized manifests and committed packaging.
evidence: .agents/quality-gates.yaml declares validate-packaging-committed as release-only, but declaration is not execution evidence.
The changed-surfaces section lists sync and validation commands as planned commands, without a candidate SHA, post-sync clean-diff assertion, tag boundary, or receipt.
docs/operator-acceptance.md lists install/update/doctor experiments but does not define the required pre-tag ordering or final artifact identity.
findings.action: Before tagging, run a candidate-bound sequence that syncs generated manifests, verifies committed packaging, asserts no post-sync diff, and records the candidate commit, generated-surface hashes, validation results, and tag identity.

findings.summary: Operator acceptance is not bound to installation of the exact release artifact in a fresh clean checkout, and doctor success is not recorded against that installed payload.
evidence: docs/operator-acceptance.md says to start from a clean tree and use a managed checkout under ~/.agents/src/charness with charness init/update, but does not require installing the exact v8.6.4 artifact.
The same page lists charness doctor and host-copy readback, but supplies no fresh-install version check, artifact hash, or installed-manifest/payload receipt.
findings.action: Install the exact v8.6.4 artifact into a disposable clean checkout or host, run doctor there, verify the installed version and generated manifest/payload from the installed location, and retain the readback evidence.

findings.summary: A mutation sample-selection failure can make the scheduled job red without opening or updating the configured regression issue.
evidence: .github/workflows/mutation-tests.yml opens or updates an issue only when steps.run.outcome or steps.summary.outcome is failure; steps.sample.outcome is absent from that condition.
The workflow body explicitly carries SAMPLE_OUTCOME and documents three states, so the reporting code recognizes sample failure while the step trigger does not.
skills/public/quality/scripts/templates/mutation-tests.yml carries the same condition, so the shipped template repeats the gap.
findings.action: Include sample failure in the issue-reporting and final-failure conditions, preserve the sample failure in the report, and add a regression test covering failed sampling with no summary artifact in both workflow copies.

findings.summary: Scheduled changed-range sampling can select a manual dispatch as its previous base, despite the workflow documentation saying dispatch cannot prove changed-line fixes.
evidence: The scheduled Plan run query filters completed runs by workflow, default branch, and success/failure, then selects the first result without filtering event to schedule.
That selected head_sha becomes MUTATION_BASE_SHA for Select mutation sample.
skills/public/quality/references/mutation-testing.md states that workflow_dispatch cannot prove the changed-line fix and that only scheduled runs compute the base SHA.
findings.action: Restrict the previous-run lookup to valid scheduled runs, or mark the base unestablished and refuse changed-line claims when no valid scheduled predecessor exists; add coverage for a dispatch run preceding a scheduled run.

findings.summary: Changes to the mutation workflow are not guaranteed to reach existing installations at release time.
evidence: skills/public/quality/references/mutation-testing.md states that the workflow is written once at first install, is never re-rendered, and has no re-render command; changing the template or schedule therefore requires manual editing or deletion and reinstall.
The release packet provides no migration, stale-workflow detection, or existing-install acceptance step for v8.6.4.
findings.action: Provide an explicit workflow migration or stale-template doctor check, and exercise both a new installation and an existing managed installation before closing the release.

counterweight_triage.concern: The release surface has no controls at all.
counterweight_triage.disposition: The packet does contain a manifest sync command, a release-only committed-packaging gate, and a serial mutate-sync-verify-publish rule; the blocker is the missing candidate-bound execution and evidence, not total absence of controls.

counterweight_triage.concern: The mutation issue reporter is broadly untested.
counterweight_triage.disposition: The packet shows substantial tests and implementation for log tails, step outcomes, body clamping, issue deduplication, and recovery candidates. Those controls should remain, but they do not cover the sample-failure trigger or scheduled-base selection.

counterweight_triage.concern: Clean-install and existing-workflow checks may be owned by an external release procedure.
counterweight_triage.disposition: If an authoritative release procedure and receipts exist outside this packet, attach them to the release record; without that evidence this review cannot treat the lock-in as closed.

next_move: Block the tag. Add and execute one release-boundary checklist covering final-candidate manifest sync, committed packaging validation, clean-diff proof, exact artifact installation, doctor and installed-payload readback, then repair and test the two scheduled mutation workflow conditions and verify migration behavior for existing installs.
non_claims: No claim is made that v8.6.4 was tagged, packaged, installed, or successfully doctored.
No claim is made that validate-packaging-committed ran on the final candidate commit.
No claim is made that a clean managed checkout read back the release artifact or host-visible payload.
No claim is made that scheduled mutation changed-line sampling has produced a valid prior-run baseline.
No claim is made that every packet path has been reviewed beyond the identity-bound semantic content provided.
